CLAUDE CODE HELPER
==================

Use your own Claude Code login (your Claude subscription) from any program, with no API key.
The helper runs on your computer and answers like the Claude Messages API at http://127.0.0.1:8787.
It was split out of the Claude Player Minecraft mod, where it lets the in-game player think on its owner's plan.

This file is written for you and for any AI agent you point at it.


HOW IT WORKS
------------
1. Your app sends a normal Messages API request (POST /v1/messages) to 127.0.0.1:8787 instead of
   api.anthropic.com.
2. The helper turns it into one turn of a warm Claude Code session running on your login. Claude Code runs
   locked down: no tools, no files, no settings, no plugins, and the helper's own system prompt.
3. The reply goes back in the API's shape (content blocks, stop_reason, usage), so SDKs and other clients
   read it as if it came from the real API.

When the next request continues the same conversation (the same messages plus new ones), the helper sends only
the new part to the session that is already warm. That skips Claude Code's startup, and once a conversation is
long enough (a few thousand tokens) earlier turns come from the prompt cache.


WHAT YOU NEED
-------------
- Java 17 or newer.
- Claude Code, installed and signed in with your own Claude account.


SETUP, STEP BY STEP (first time)
--------------------------------
1. Install Java 17 or newer.
   - Download it from https://adoptium.net (Temurin 17 or 21) and install it.
   - Check it: open a new terminal (Windows: PowerShell) and type
         java -version
     It should say version "17" or higher. If it says 1.8 or another old version, an old Java comes first on
     your PATH: set JAVA_HOME to the new Java's folder (the start scripts use JAVA_HOME when it is set).

2. Install Claude Code and sign in.
   - Windows (PowerShell):    irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
   - macOS or Linux:          curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
     (These are Anthropic's official installers. Their Claude Code documentation has the details.)
   - Open a new terminal, type
         claude
     and follow the sign-in. Use your own Claude account.
   - Confirm it works: ask it something ("say hi"), then type /exit. You can also run
         claude auth status
     and look for "loggedIn": true.

3. Unzip the helper anywhere, for example to your Documents folder. Then start it:
   - Windows: double-click start-helper.bat, or from a terminal in that folder:
         start-helper.bat --token pick-a-long-secret
   - macOS or Linux, from a terminal in that folder:
         ./start-helper.sh --token pick-a-long-secret
   - Or directly:
         java -jar claude-code-helper.jar --token pick-a-long-secret
   Use --token. With it, only programs that know the token can use your plan.
   Leave the window open: the helper runs until you stop it.

4. Check that it runs.
   - Open http://127.0.0.1:8787/health in your browser. You should see "status": "ok", the claude path,
     and "signed_in": true.
   - Then one real test. Save this as hello.json in any folder:
         {"model": "claude-haiku-5-5", "max_tokens": 200,
          "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in three words."}]}
     and from a terminal in that folder run (Windows: in PowerShell type curl.exe, in cmd type curl):
         curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/messages -H "content-type: application/json" -H "x-api-key: pick-a-long-secret" -d "@hello.json"
     The answer is JSON with "type": "message" and your reply in "content". It takes a few seconds.

5. Point your own AIs and apps at it.
   - Base URL:  http://127.0.0.1:8787     (clients add /v1/messages themselves)
   - API key:   your token (or, without --token, any string at all)
   - Many tools also read the environment variables ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

   Python (pip install anthropic):
       import anthropic
       client = anthropic.Anthropic(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8787", api_key="pick-a-long-secret")
       reply = client.messages.create(model="claude-haiku-5-5", max_tokens=500,
                                      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}])
       print(reply.content[0].text)

   TypeScript or JavaScript (npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk):
       import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk";
       const client = new Anthropic({ baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:8787", apiKey: "pick-a-long-secret" });
       const reply = await client.messages.create({ model: "claude-haiku-5-5", max_tokens: 500,
                                                    messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello!" }] });
       console.log(reply.content[0].text);

   Plain HTTP, from any language:
       POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/messages
       Content-Type: application/json
       x-api-key: pick-a-long-secret          (or  Authorization: Bearer pick-a-long-secret)
       {"model": "claude-haiku-5-5", "max_tokens": 500, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}

6. Stop it: press Ctrl+C in its window (or close the window). It stops its Claude Code processes on the way
   out; if it is killed hard, the next start cleans up any it left behind.

Options:
    --port <n>          port on 127.0.0.1 (default 8787)
    --token <secret>    require this key. Or set the environment variable CLAUDE_HELPER_TOKEN instead,
                        which keeps it out of the process list.
    --model <id>        the model when a request names none
    --claude <path>     the claude program, if it isn't found on its own
    --effort <level>    low, medium, high, xhigh or max
    --timeout <s>       seconds one reply may take (default 300)
    --idle-minutes <n>  stop warm sessions unused this long (default 10)
    --max-sessions <n>  requests at the same time (default 4)


TROUBLESHOOTING
---------------
- "claude not found": install Claude Code (step 2) and open a new terminal, or start the helper with
  --claude "C:\path\to\claude.exe". The helper looks on PATH, then in %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin (Windows) or
  ~/.local/bin. An npm install (claude.cmd) isn't picked up on its own; the native installer is the tested way.
- "isn't signed in" (HTTP 401 authentication_error, or "signed_in": false in /health): run claude in a
  terminal and sign in again, then retry. No restart of the helper is needed.
- "Port 8787 is in use": the helper is probably already running in another window. Or start it with
  --port 8788 and use that port in your base URL.
- The first reply is slow: starting Claude Code takes a few seconds. The helper keeps one spare session
  started ahead, and later replies in the same conversation reuse the warm session. Expect 1 to 5 seconds a turn.
- UnsupportedClassVersionError: your Java is older than 17 (see step 1).
- HTTP 401 with your token set: the key your app sends doesn't match --token.
- HTTP 529 overloaded_error: more requests at once than --max-sessions. SDKs retry these on their own.
- HTTP 403 permission_error: the request came from a web page on another site, or was addressed to a host
  name other than 127.0.0.1 or localhost. That is refused on purpose.


WHAT WORKS AND WHAT DOESN'T
---------------------------
Works:
- POST /v1/messages with system (a string or text blocks), multi-turn messages, and usage in every reply.
- Images: base64 PNG and JPEG, in user messages and inside tool results.
- Tools (your own, with input_schema): emulated. Claude Code itself runs with no tools; the helper asks it for
  a structured answer and turns that into standard tool_use blocks with fresh ids and stop_reason "tool_use".
  You run the tool and send a tool_result back as usual. tool_choice auto, any, tool and none work, and so
  does disable_parallel_tool_use.
- stream: true works, but the events arrive all at once when the reply is finished (standard message_start ...
  message_stop events), so there is no typing effect.
- Models: "model" is passed to Claude Code, so use a model id or alias Claude Code accepts on your plan.
- GET /health: the claude path, its version, and whether it is signed in.

Accepted but ignored: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k, stop_sequences, metadata, thinking, service_tier,
and cache_control (Claude Code caches on its own).

Not supported (you get a clear 400 error): image URLs, GIF and WebP, PDFs and other document blocks, Anthropic's
server tools (web search and the like), and assistant prefill (the last message must be from the user).
There is no /v1/models, token counting or batches endpoint.

Latency: a few seconds per turn (measured 1.2 to 4.8 s with claude-haiku-5-5), more for long answers.
One request at a time per conversation; up to --max-sessions conversations in parallel.


YOUR PLAN'S LIMITS
------------------
Every request counts against your Claude plan's usage limits, exactly as if you typed it into Claude Code.
A program that loops can use up your limit quickly. When the limit is reached, requests fail with HTTP 429
until it resets.


SAFETY
------
- The helper only listens on 127.0.0.1 (this computer). Never expose it to a network: no port forwarding,
  no tunnels, no 0.0.0.0, no sharing it with other people.
- Use --token. Without it, any program running on this computer can use your plan through the helper.
- It never reads your Claude credentials; Claude Code keeps its own sign-in. It removes any ANTHROPIC_* and
  cloud-billing variables from Claude Code's environment, so it always uses your subscription login.
- Its log lines carry request ids, the model, timings, token counts and stop reasons only: never your prompts,
  images or the token.


TERMS
-----
This is for personal use on your own account. Before you build anything shared on it (other people using it,
a public app, a service), check Anthropic's terms for Claude subscriptions and Claude Code. Shared or
commercial use generally belongs on the Claude API with an API key.


USING IT AS A JAVA LIBRARY
--------------------------
The same jar is a plain Java library (Gson is bundled inside). A warm Claude Code session, no server needed:

    import com.example.claudecodehelper.*;
    import java.nio.file.*;
    import java.util.List;

    public class Demo {
        public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
            try (ClaudeCode cc = ClaudeCode.builder().model("claude-haiku-5-5").systemPrompt("You are terse.").build();
                 ClaudeCode.Session chat = cc.open()) {
                Reply r = chat.send("Name three colours.");
                System.out.println(r.text() + "  (" + r.usage().output() + " tokens out)");
                r = chat.send("Three more.");                       // same warm session, no restart
                System.out.println(r.text());
                r = chat.send(List.of(Blocks.text("What is in this picture?"),
                                      Blocks.png(Files.readAllBytes(Path.of("picture.png")))));
                System.out.println(r.text());
            }
        }
    }

    javac -cp claude-code-helper.jar Demo.java
    java -cp "claude-code-helper.jar;." Demo        (on macOS or Linux use : instead of ;)

Builder options: claudePath, model, effort, systemPrompt, jsonSchema (structured output, read back with
reply.structured()), turnTimeout, idleMinutes, maxSessions. Each reply has text(), structured(), usage(),
rateLimit() (Claude Code's plan-usage reading, sent on a session's first turn) and stopReason().
For stateless callers (like the server), cc.lease(options, history) continues a warm session whose
conversation the new history extends, or starts a fresh one.
